Goal: `Server/Transcripts.mjs`, a Node-only script (no LLM calls) that reads the raw Claude SDK transcripts and writes a condensed, factual "essence" file into the matching task folder, so sessions finally say what they were about, what they touched, and what they cost.

Facts you can rely on:
- Raw transcripts: `C:\Users\mike\.claude\projects\<project dir>\<session uuid>.jsonl`. Project dirs start with `C--Code-lew42-` or `c--Code-lew42-` (case varies). 9,720 files, 8.1 GB total; 301 modified in the last 2 days. `Server/SessionIndex.mjs` has `static transcripts()` that already maps session uuid → path; reuse it, and reuse `SessionIndex.module_of(file)` for module tags.
- Each task folder under public/framework/ai/sessions has a task.jsonl whose line 1 is `{"assign":{"session_id":...}}`. That is the join key. SessionIndex.reduce reads these.
- Transcript records are JSONL with `type` in user / assistant / attachment / queue-operation / prompt_snapshot / last-prompt / total_tokens_reminder / ... Look at two real files first (one tiny 56 KB, one big like 24f68eac-0d5f-4343-98fc-95e99a69e6e3.jsonl, 5.7 MB) and write down the exact shapes you see before coding.

What to keep per session (one `essence.jsonl` next to task.jsonl, one JSON line per kept event, plus a first line `{"summary":{...}}`):
- owner/user prompts: `type:user` records whose message.content has text blocks (NOT tool_result blocks). Keep full text; this is the essence.
- assistant text blocks
